title: [WT-08T] Tests: held-out acceptance cases for worktree completion landing
definitionOfDone: scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh and scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1 exist; `--list` prints at least 12 cases, each tagged local or remote, with the same case names in both files.
Every case named in the description is present and asserts on git state (refs, reflog, parents, file bytes), not only on log text.
Against current code `bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh` exits non-zero with every case failing on its assertion (no harness crash); `--only local` and `--only remote` select the tagged subsets.

The ps1 twin parses (powershell -NoProfile -Command "$null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1',[ref]$null,[ref]$e); if ($e) { exit 1 }") and is red the same way on a Windows seat.
No file outside scripts/tests/worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} is modified; the verification command exits 0.
taskRails: WT-08T size exception. WT-08T (task-c12f9463b68c44a18cc460a7e9460247) is the epic's held-out acceptance suite for worktree completion landing. Its plan names 15 cases (8 local, 7 remote), above the DoD's minimum of 12, and WT-08 and WT-09 must pass them unchanged. Its only files are two new ones: scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh and scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1. The .ps1 runs the node suite embedded in the .sh, so each case is written once. Together the two files may add at most 700 lines, counted by git diff --numstat with comments and blank lines included, which is over the 400 net-LOC review cap. No other file may change. This waives size only: every DoD item, the epic rails, substantive QA and fresh verification still apply in full.

implementationPlan.description:
Harness core: both launchers, the shared node suite's runner, and helpers. Cases come in steps 2-3.

Layout: every case is written once, in a node suite embedded in the .sh. The .ps1 extracts and runs it, so no third file is needed (DoD 5).

scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh:
- `#!/usr/bin/env bash` and `set -euo pipefail`.
- Header comment: the suite pins design §2.2/§2.3/§2.6/§2.7/§2.9 plus this row's two WT-S comments; it is held out for WT-08/WT-09 and stays out of CI until WT-09; usage is `--list` and `--only local|remote`; the seams it relies on are in planningNotes.
- Resolve ROOT_DIR and WRAPPER=scripts/moe-agent.sh. Resolve node from MOE_NODE_COMMAND, else PATH; if missing, print `ERROR harness: node not found` and exit 2.
- Make TMP_DIR with mktemp and set an EXIT trap that removes it.
- Install the shared fake proxy exactly as postflight.sh does, `cp "$ROOT_DIR/scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js" "$FAKE_PROXY"`. Never write a private proxy body.
- Write the suite with `cat > "$SUITE" <<'WTJS'` ... `WTJS`. Keep both marker lines byte-exact, because the .ps1 extracts this block.
- Run `"$NODE" "$SUITE" sh "$WRAPPER" "$FAKE_PROXY" "$TMP_DIR" "$(command -v bash)" "$@"` without exec, so the trap still runs, and exit with its status.

scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1:
- Save it as UTF-8 with a BOM and LF line endings, like postflight.ps1.
- Forward $args (--list, --only <tag>) unchanged.
- Resolve node (else exit 2), make a temp root under [IO.Path]::GetTempPath(), and Copy-Item the shared fake proxy the way postflight.ps1 does.
- Extract the suite: read worktree-landing.sh from $PSScriptRoot and take the lines strictly between the line `cat > "$SUITE" <<'WTJS'` and the next line that is exactly `WTJS`. If either marker is missing, print `ERROR harness: suite markers not found` and exit 2. Write the body with [IO.File]::WriteAllText (UTF-8, no BOM).
- Keep a literal `$expectedCases` array of every `<tag> <name>` line and compare it with the suite's `--list` output. On any difference, print `ERROR harness: case list drift` and exit 2. This makes DoD 1's "same case names in both files" literal and checked.
- Run `& node $suite ps1 $wrapper $fakeProxy $tempRoot <path of the running powershell exe> @args` and keep $LASTEXITCODE. In a finally block, remove the temp root after checking its path prefix. Exit with that code.

Suite runner (plain CommonJS with node:assert/strict, inside the heredoc):
- argv: platform (sh|ps1), wrapper, fake proxy, tmp root, engine, then flags.
  - `--list` prints one `<tag> <name>` line per case and exits 0, before any prerequisite check.
  - `--only local|remote` filters; any other value exits 2. An unknown flag exits 2.
- Registry: `const CASES = [[tag, name, fn], ...]`, with names matching [a-z0-9-]+.
- Prerequisites, checked before running any case: git 2.38 or later (merge-tree --write-tree), parsed from `git version`. If unmet, print `ERROR harness: ...` and exit 2. Never SKIP silently: once WT-09 registers the file in CI, a skip would read as green.
- Run each case in its own dir under the tmp root. The dir name contains a space, to catch quoting bugs, but keep names short for Windows path limits. Wrap each case in try/catch:
  - success → `PASS <tag> <name>`;
  - an assertion failure (err.code === 'ERR_ASSERTION') → `FAIL <tag> <name>: <first line of the message>`;
  - anything else → `ERROR <tag> <name>: <message>`, plus the first stack lines.
  After the cases, print one summary line that starts with neither FAIL nor ERROR, for example `worktree-landing: P passed, F failed, E errors`. Exit 2 if there is any ERROR, else 1 if there is any FAIL, else 0.
- Error handling contract: setup and fixture helpers throw plain Errors, which count as ERROR (a harness bug). Only expectations about the landing use assert, which counts as FAIL.

Helpers:
- git(dir, ...args): spawnSync git and throw an Error carrying stderr on a non-zero exit (setup only). tryGit returns {status, stdout, stderr}, for assertions.
- project(caseDir, {remote}) builds P = <caseDir>/project:
  - `git init -q -b main`; config user.name/user.email, core.autocrlf false, commit.gpgsign false and core.logAllRefUpdates always.
  - Files:
    - shared.txt with 10 numbered lines;
    - .moe/project.json `{"id":"proj-wt","name":"worktree-landing","settings":{}}`, with no qualityGate, so no case takes the land lease (WT-S comment);
    - a tracked .moe/tasks/task-postflight.json, as on a real board;
    - a .gitignore with `/.moe/*`, `!/.moe/project.json`, `!/.moe/tasks/` and `/.worktrees/`, so the fake proxy's runtime files never dirty P.
  - Commit `seed` on main; that commit is B0. Then `git switch -q -c moe/control`, because WT-04 stops a worktree-mode worker unless HEAD is refs/heads/moe/control (§6.5).
  - Write .moe/daemon.json and .moe/messages/chan-general.jsonl as postflight.sh does.
  - With remote:
    - make a bare <caseDir>/origin.git with receive.denyNonFastForwards true and core.logAllRefUpdates always;
    - `remote add origin`, `push -q origin main`, `fetch -q origin`.
- peerCommit(P, ref, edits) makes one plumbing commit on `ref` with a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE (read-tree, hash-object -w, update-index --cacheinfo, write-tree, commit-tree -p, then update-ref with the old value) and returns the sha.
- peerPush(caseDir, edits) clones origin into <caseDir>/peer, commits, does a plain `git push origin main` and returns the sha.
- seat(P, opts) runs the wrapper once.
  - Fake CLI: a node script, generated from a template, that writes opts.edits into W = path.join(P,'.worktrees','task-postflight') by absolute path and then runs the optional opts.during JS snippet. The template gives the snippet P, W, the real git path and the fail-file path as constants. Launch it the way the frozen suite does: a bash script on sh, a .cmd on ps1.
  - Env: process.env with every MOE_*, CLAUDE_* and GIT_* key deleted (a seat's own env leaks in otherwise). Then set:
    - MOE_PROXY_PATH and MOE_NODE_COMMAND=process.execPath;
    - MOE_DISABLE_HEARTBEAT=1 and MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION=off;
    - HOME and USERPROFILE = <caseDir>/home;
    - FAKE_TASK_STATUS=REVIEW;
    - the worktree claim knob (below);
    - opts.env.
  - Argv, as in the frozen suite:
    - sh: `bash <wrapper> --project P --worker-id worker-wt --role worker --team Smoke --no-start-daemon --command <cli> --no-loop --poll-interval 0`;
    - ps1: `-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <wrapper> -Project P -WorkerId worker-wt -Role worker -Team Smoke -NoStartDaemon -Command <cli> -NoLoop -PollInterval 0`.
  - spawnSync with a timeout of MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 180) seconds. Return {status, log}. A timeout is assert.fail naming the case.
- Worktree claim knob. WT-04 adds the fake-proxy knob that makes claim_next_task and get_context return a worktree `workspace`; WT-05's planner asked for FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE, a JSON object returned verbatim (msg-ef695be0). Read scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js and use the knob as shipped, with {"mode":"worktree","path":W,"branch":"moe/task/task-postflight","target":"main"}. If WT-04 shipped none, generate a small adapter proxy into the tmp root at runtime. It runs the shared proxy and adds that `workspace` to those two replies, plus workspace and workspaceMode to its attempt record. Never edit the shared proxy (DoD 5).
- Readers:
  - rows(P) parses P/.moe/evidence-rpcs.jsonl ({tool,args});
  - completions(P) = record_commit rows with kind completion;
  - finals(P) = finalize_attempt rows;
  - journal(P) = the JSON at <`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` of P>/moe/receipt/task-postflight.json, or null.
- Hooks. hook(caseDir, js) writes a .cjs file and returns `node "<path with forward slashes>"`, a command that is valid under both bash -c and cmd /c. Cases pass it as MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_HOOK_PRE_UPDATE_REF.

Prove the suite is red on both platforms, then run the verification command once.

1. sh red run: run `bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh`. Every listed case must print FAIL, with a landing expectation in its message. No case may be red only because of a timeout, a missing fixture or a setup error. Fix the harness until that holds.

2. ps1 (DoD 4):
   - Parse check: `powershell -NoProfile -Command "$null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1',[ref]$null,[ref]$e); if ($e) { exit 1 }"`.
   - Full Windows run: from WSL, cd into a Windows-drive dir and run `env -u <each MOE_*/CLAUDE_* var> MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File '<D:\...>\scripts\tests\worktree-landing.ps1'` (mem:gotcha-qa-ps1-postflight-from-wsl).
   - Expect exit 1, the same case names, every case FAIL, and no ERROR.
   - If no Windows host is reachable, say so in the evidence; do not claim DoD 4.

3. Verification command. Run it from the repo root; its fresh output is the complete_task evidence:

L=$(mktemp) && R=$(mktemp) && bash -n scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh --list > "$L" && cat "$L" && test "$(grep -cE '^(local|remote) [a-z0-9-]+$' "$L")" -ge 12 && test -n "$(bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh --list --only local)" && test -z "$(bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh --list --only local | grep -v '^local ')" && test -n "$(bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh --list --only remote)" && test -z "$(bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh --list --only remote | grep -v '^remote ')" && { bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh > "$R" 2>&1; test $? -eq 1; } && ! grep -q '^ERROR ' "$R" && test "$(grep -c '^FAIL ' "$R")" -eq "$(wc -l < "$L")" && tail -n 25 "$R" && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh

What it checks:
- It holds the description's checks: bash -n, --list, the red run and parity-check.
- The red check is strict: exit exactly 1, one FAIL line per listed case, and no ERROR line (DoD 3, "no harness crash").
- It also checks the case count (at least 12) and both --only filters (DoD 1 and DoD 3).
- If parity-check fails only because a peer is mid-edit in scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}, also run it on a HEAD snapshot (`S=$(mktemp -d) && git archive HEAD scripts | tar -x -C "$S" && (cd "$S" && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh)`) and report both runs.

4. `git status --porcelain` must show no change from this task outside the two files (DoD 5). Board records are not task files.

Do not register either file in CI. WT-09 does that.

comments.content:
Follow-up to the WT-S revision comment above. WT-08 and WT-09 must pass these files before WT-11 adds the unlanded route, and WT-11 must still pass them unchanged afterwards. That fixes what each case may assert:
- Cases 1 (QA's race) and 6 (diverged), for the seat that loses:
  - assert git state and the log code (MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED or MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED);
  - assert no `record_commit` with `pushed: true` and no `landed` finalize;
  - do NOT assert the `finalize_attempt unlanded` call. WT-11's own cases cover it.
- Case 4 (unknown outcome): assert no finalize at all. That holds both before and after WT-11.
- Run every case with no qualityGate, so no lease call is involved (revised §2.2 L3).

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Spike self-review correction (docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §2.2 L8/L9, §2.6; section numbers unchanged). Where this differs from the description or my earlier comments, this comment wins.

Contract changes:
1. L9 push classification, on the target's porcelain line:
   - ` `, `*` or `=`: published.
   - `!` with `[rejected]`: the round ends.
   - `!` with `[remote rejected]`: MOE_PUSH_FAILED, unlanded `remote`, no more rounds.
   - `[remote failure]`, a transport error or no line: reconcile_push.
2. reconcile_push (§2.6) settles an unanswered push with a fetch:
   - The tip contains C: published.
   - The tip is neither B nor contains C: C can never apply (the remote takes C only as a fast-forward from B, and nobody force-pushes, rail 1). MOE_PUSH_FAILED, and the round ends.
   - The tip is still B: the SAME C is pushed again, up to 3 pushes in all. A repeat's refusal decides nothing; only the fetch does.
   - The fetch fails, or the tip is still B after the third push: unknown.
3. Replay never re-lands. It settles the journaled C with reconcile_push and never merges, gates or builds a new commit.

Cases to add or adjust. All are tagged remote and assert git state and codes only, per e07af02f:
(a) Unanswered push, tip still B: the git shim fails the first push transport-wise without applying it. The same C is pushed again, and main ends at that C (same sha), with exactly one completion on main.
(b) Remote rejected: a pre-receive hook on the bare remote refuses the push. Main is unchanged, exactly one push runs, MOE_PUSH_FAILED is printed, and no second round starts.
(c) Unknown then replay: the replayed landing publishes the journaled C itself (same sha), not a new merge.
(d) Unanswered push while a peer lands: main never contains C, and MOE_PUSH_FAILED is printed. A later round may land a new commit on the peer's tip.

Also:
- Every worktree completion now writes a receipt journal, including gate-less ones (`candidateId: null`, L8), so a case may assert that the journal exists after an unknown outcome.
- Keep fixtures gate-less unless a case needs a gate: while a qualityGate is set, L6 runs on every landing (qualityGateScope is ignored) and L3 takes the lease.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Two new files, scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh and its .ps1 twin, run one node suite: the .sh embeds it and the .ps1 extracts it. The suite drives the real moe-agent.sh or moe-agent.ps1 post-flight in worktree mode against scratch repos, and the shared fake proxy answers the claim with a worktree workspace. It holds 15 cases, 8 tagged local and 7 tagged remote, that pin landing to main per design §2.2/§2.3/§2.6/§2.7/§2.9 and the WT-S comments. Each case asserts git state first and codes or ledger rows second. `--list` prints `<tag> <name>` lines and `--only local|remote` filters. Exit codes: 0 when every case passes, 1 when there are assertion failures only, and 2 on any harness error. Against today's code every case FAILs, so the exit is 1.
acceptanceCriteria: `--list` prints at least 12 `<tag> <name>` lines, and the .ps1 checks that its literal list matches.
Every case named in the description and the WT-S comments is present and asserts refs, reflogs, parents or file bytes.
Against current code: exit 1, one FAIL line per case, and no ERROR line.
The .ps1 parses, and on Windows it is red the same way.
No file other than the two new ones changes.
invariants: The suite never edits postflight-fake-proxy.js, the wrappers or CI.
Failure injection is deterministic: a PATH-first shim whose fail file is re-read on every call. No sleeps.
A harness fault is ERROR (exit 2), never FAIL, and missing prerequisites never SKIP to exit 0.
Every case cleans up its temp dirs and never touches the developer's HOME or the real repository.

scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1: launcher, suite extraction, literal case list

the existing MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_HOOK_PRE_UPDATE_REF seam, the receipt journal and the MOE_RESCUE_REF line

moe-agent.sh runs receipt_replay right after the pre-flight claim.
WT-04 adds the fake-proxy worktree claim knob; WT-05's planner requested FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Each alternative, and why it was rejected:
- Duplicating the node suite in both files, the way postflight.{sh,ps1} duplicate the frozen suite. That doubles the line count and invites drift. Here the .ps1 extracts the .sh's heredoc and pins the case list.
- A separate shared scripts/tests/worktree-landing.cjs, the postflight-owner-guard.cjs pattern. DoD 5 allows no third file.
- Real two-seat runs with a second task id. postflight-fake-proxy.js hard-codes task-postflight/attempt-postflight, and DoD 5 forbids editing it. Peers are therefore simulated: the PRE_UPDATE_REF hook, direct plumbing commits or peer-clone pushes, and an opts.during CLI snippet for QA's race. The race case does not cover "A finalizes landed", and the case comment says so.
- An ext:: transport helper for failure injection. It sees no client argv (the force-flag evidence) and needs protocol.ext.allow. The WT-S comment prescribes a PATH shim anyway.
- GIT_TRACE as argv evidence. A landing that sanitizes GIT_* env would lose it and fail a correct implementation.
- A git.cmd shim on Windows. cmd mangles ^ (HEAD^{tree}). git.ps1 was verified to resolve first in PS 5.1 with args intact.
- Simulating push-after-apply with a plain real push. That push updates refs/remotes/origin/main, so the shim restores the tracking refs.
- A SKIP exit 0 when prerequisites are missing (postflight.sh's convention). A held-out landing gate must never read green unrun, so missing prerequisites exit 2.
- Splitting the row. The DoD is one whole deliverable (at least 12 cases, the same names in both files), so I asked for a size waiver instead (prop-72430aa5).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Facts the plan relies on: - scripts/tests/postflight.sh embeds its frozen-candidate node suite in a heredoc and runs it as `node suite sh|ps1 wrapper proxy tmp engine`. Its argv, its env (MOE_PROXY_PATH, MOE_NODE_COMMAND, MOE_DISABLE_HEARTBEAT, FAKE_TASK_STATUS=REVIEW, HOME/USERPROFILE) and its .cmd CLI launcher are the model for seat(). - postflight-fake-proxy.js logs {tool,args} to

/.moe/evidence-rpcs.jsonl for record_commit, finalize_attempt and record_delivery_receipt. It flips the attempt to finalizing on the second REVIEW get_context. - MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_HOOK_PRE_UPDATE_REF is today's one-shot race seam: sh `(cd $MOE_TOP && bash -c)` at moe-agent.sh ~4848, ps1 `cmd /c` at ~4959. It fires between commit-tree and update-ref. - receipt_replay runs right after the pre-flight claim, even when the claim returns hasNext:false (sh ~6728). - receipt_report's fields are candidateId, target, targetBefore, targetAfter, landedRevision and pushResult. - A rescue logs `MOE_RESCUE_REF task= ref= sha= reason=`. - .gitattributes forces LF everywhere. postflight.ps1 carries a UTF-8 BOM. - WT-04 enforces HEAD = refs/heads/moe/control for a worktree-mode worker (§6.5).
planningNotes.risks:
Seams WT-08 and WT-09 must honour. I post them as comments on those rows; QA should check that this suite needs nothing beyond them:
- S1: the worktree completion arm runs MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_HOOK_PRE_UPDATE_REF once per landing, then unsets it. It fires after L8's journal and before L9's publication (the local CAS, or the push), with today's cwd and shell.
- S2: L8 journals every worktree completion, gated or not, at <git common dir>/moe/receipt/<taskId>.json. It uses receipt_report's fields: targetBefore = B, landedRevision = targetAfter = C, and pushResult `push unknown: ...` while the outcome is unknown.
- S3: ps1 fetch and push call bare `git` (PowerShell resolution), never git.exe by path, cmd or node. On sh, any PATH git.
- S4: the ledger rows:
  - a successful completion is committed, with sha C, ref refs/heads/main, and pushed true only on remote proof;
  - M == B^{tree} gives outcome nothing with MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT;
  - finalize landed carries landedRevision C.
- S5: the codes in the design: MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_CONFLICT, MOE_LAND_TARGET_CHECKED_OUT, MOE_WORKTREE_BOARD_PATH, MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED, MOE_PUSH_FAILED, MOE_PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED, and reason=push-unknown.

Other risks:
- WT-04's knob name for the worktree claim may differ from FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE. Use whatever shipped, else the runtime adapter.
- The WSL environment leaks into Windows runs. Unset MOE_*/CLAUDE_*, use a Windows-drive cwd, and allow a 180 s timeout.
- Runtime: 15 cases with up to 2 wrapper runs each, likely 5-10 minutes in total.
- Size: the plan expects about 500-600 lines against a 700 cap, pending human approval of prop-72430aa5.
